author: Mark Atwood
text:
Filing as human because this is the bead's framing 'kit's first major opportunity to convert tuple-of-two into named-struct-of-N before the type ossifies' — i.e. it explicitly proposes a workspace-wide breaking change.

Scope: 147 'Result<(Value, Vec<Invocation>), JmapError>' sites across 11 crates (mail-server alone has ~80, mostly in email.rs / mailbox.rs / sieve.rs / submission.rs). Mechanical refactor but every JmapHandler impl + every register_*_handlers macro closure has to change. Workspace AGENTS.md is explicit: 'Prefer non-breaking changes. Reshape only when the workspace is bumping a major.'

Options:
  (a) Land HandlerOutput { primary, extra_invocations } struct under a workspace major-version bump. Single consolidated propagation pass. ~50 files. Catches every future field non-breakingly.
  (b) Hold for the next planned major bump. File a follow-up bead under that major's epic to land this then.
  (c) Land HandlerOutput AS the canonical-server canonical-template (single-source-of-truth foundation crate per AGENTS.md), keep the legacy tuple alias for one transition cycle via a wrapper closure or From impl, then sweep extension crates one at a time. Two-step migration, no atomic major bump.

Recommendation: (b). The HandlerFuture shape ossifying is a real cost, but the immediate work is correctness fixes (.1, .2, .3 just landed) and the workspace has no current major-bump driver. Forcing a workspace-wide major bump for this one structural improvement (when the actual unbound-growth field is hypothetical) inverts the priority. The bead's reasoning is sound — the surface WILL keep growing — but it doesn't propose a concrete first user. Land it when the first concrete user shows up (e.g. handler-emitted metrics for a feature bead), under that feature's epic, not as a free-floating canonical-template churn.

Awaiting human decision on (a) / (b) / (c).
